reviews.question:
With the rapid development of communication technology; e.g. smart phones, tablets and other mobile devices, some people believe that the disadvantages outweigh the advantages.
To what extent do you agree or disagree?
reviews.originalEssay:
The contemporary era is witnessing swift breakthroughs in communication technology, characterized by the ubiquity of handheld devices. In this essay, however, I am of the opposite school of thought.
           Admittedly, one might argue that this shift has sparked concerns regarding its potential downsides, but it is easily handled. On this side of debate, people also cite that social network platforms, in itself, make it relatively easy to fake identities while users are vulnerable to cyber attacks, which leads to the increasing number of reports of online scams using hacked social media accounts or stolen personal identification numbers. However, this line of reasoning is not sound, identity theft, which has always been a problem, not primarily due to the lack of security of a particular networking site or application but rather due to users’ carelessness. With proper care and attention, social network users can protect themselves from fraud by several easy actions, such as adjusting privacy control settings and turning on two-step verification, greatly reduce the incidence of identity theft overall.
            To add further credence to my assertion, I note the appreciable benefits of social media. By facilitating long-distance communication, it enables people to connect no matter where they are. Individuals from all corners of the globe now can interact instantly through messaging or video calls, which conversely was rarely the case in the past, when people had limited chances to engage with others outside their immediate surroundings. This can be easily seen in the business sector: virtual meetings and cross-border collaboration become the norm. With video conferencing allowing participants from different time zones to join live discussions, it is particularly beneficial for startups and small businesses aiming to expand internationally by reducing travel costs and speeding up decision-making.
             In conclusion, despite some undeniable drawbacks, I strongly believe this trend is beneficial for society and all the world.
reviews.overall: Em giữ đúng lập trường và đủ chuỗi ý Cô giao: thừa nhận rủi ro rồi phản biện bằng cách bảo vệ tài khoản, sau đó phát triển lợi ích liên lạc xa với ví dụ kinh doanh. Bài cần sửa vài câu ghép chưa hoàn chỉnh để quan hệ phản biện và kết quả rõ, chính xác hơn.

reviews.question:
Some people think that the increasing use of computers and mobile phones for communication has a negative effect on young people’s reading and writing skills.
To what extent do you agree or disagree?
reviews.originalEssay:
There is an opinion that technology services, such as computer or mobile phone, are replacing face-to-face contact in this century, and it does harmful to young people's abilities to reading and writing. Personally, I am of the same school of thought.

On the one hand, this trend bring some disadvantages for youths' reading skills. Initially, what they read on these devices, in bite-sized snippets, affect their ability to stay focused for a larger period of time, obviously leading to comprehension problems when it comes to longer texts. Furthermore, notifications pushed to their phones from social media platforms to make matters worse and distract them when they try to read, which further affect their reading comprehension.

On the other hand, the heavy reliance on mobile devices often erodes individuals' writing proficiency, as features like predictive text discourage active spelling and complex sentence construction. Chief among them is the rise in informal language used in online interactions, characterized by the use of slang, abbreviations and emojis, not adhere strictly to grammar and punctuation rules for the sake of convenience in communicating. Moreover, relying blindly on functions, such as text predictions and auto correction on computers and smartphones, people easily to make spelling mistakes, which lead to such colloquial language and grammar mistakes much less acceptable in more formal contexts, say, academic essays, business proposals and professional correspondence.                                      In conclusion, I strongly believe that excessive usage of modern gadgets undermines the literacy skills of the younger generation. By fostering a reliance on bite-sized content and automated features like auto-correct, technology impairs deep reading comprehension and erodes formal writing standards.
reviews.overall: Em bám đúng hướng đồng ý và đã triển khai đủ hai mảng reading và writing theo dàn ý Cô giao. Chuỗi ý về đoạn đọc khá rõ, còn đoạn viết giữ đủ các nguyên nhân và hệ quả nhưng có vài câu bị gãy cấu trúc. Lỗi chia động từ, thiếu động từ chính và cách nối mệnh đề làm người đọc khó theo dõi ở những chỗ quan trọng. Em hãy sửa lại toàn bài theo các chú thích rồi nộp lại để Cô kiểm tra độ chính xác.

reviews.question:
The Internet has transformed the way information is shared and consumed, but it has also created problems that did not exist before.
What are the most serious problems associated with the Internet and what are the possible solutions?
reviews.originalEssay:
The Internet has revolutionized how information is shared and consumed globally; however, it has also given rise to unprecedented challenges. The most serious issues stemming from this digital shift are cyberbullying and online manipulation, but feasible solutions involving awareness campaigns and regulatory frameworks can effectively address these concerns.

On the one hand, the proliferation of the Internet has brought severe problems in its wake, primarily in the form of cyberbullying and information manipulation. Regarding the former, social media platforms are frequently used to spread lies and rumors to thousands of people in an instant. Due to the invasive nature of this online harassment, victims often find it virtually impossible to escape, leading to extreme emotional suffering. Furthermore, there is hardly any regulation on the types of information posted on the Internet, allowing malicious individuals to exploit this freedom to their advantage. A prime example of this can be seen in the way the Trump administration won the US presidential election in large measure by strategically running targeted advertisements on Facebook to influence public opinion.

On the other hand, actionable measures can be taken to bring these problems under control. First, mounting widespread awareness campaigns about the dangers associated with Internet usage, especially cyberbullying, is essential. Celebrities who are widely trusted by the public can leverage their platforms to spread impactful messages, such as sharing stories about the severe psychological distress that a bullied individual has to endure. Conversely, political and digital manipulation is far more difficult to tackle because introducing legislation to strictly check social media content and adverts might in itself be considered a form of censorship. Deciding what is deemed illegal can be highly subjective and risks infringing upon freedom of speech. Nevertheless, governments should establish clear, transparent legal guidelines focused on data privacy and truth in advertising to curb malicious practices without stifling open discourse.

In conclusion, while cyberbullying and digital manipulation present major threats in the modern age, they can be mitigated through elevated public awareness led by influential figures and carefully balanced government regulation.

reviews.question:
Some people believe that reading stories from a book is better than watching TV or playing computer games for children.
To what extent do you agree or disagree?
reviews.originalEssay:
It is often argued that reading storybooks offers greater benefits to children’s development than consuming television programs or playing video games. I completely agree with this view, as reading stories is far more effective in enriching language skills and fostering creative imagination than the other two forms of entertainment.                                              On the one hand, reading literary stories provides a superior foundation for language acquisition compared to television and gaming. When children engage with books, they actively absorb rich vocabulary, nuanced expressions, and complex grammatical structures, which significantly enhances their linguistic proficiency. In contrast, while TV shows and movies do expose children to new words, the spoken language used in broadcasting is often colloquial and lacks the syntactic complexity found in print. Similarly, although video games may require players to read textual instructions or dialogue to complete missions, this vocabulary is strictly confined to the game’s context. It fails to expose young minds to the diverse facets of real-life experiences that literature naturally encompasses.                           On the other hand, storybooks are uniquely powerful in stimulating a child's imagination and creativity. When reading a fictional tale, children must mentally conjure up their own images to visualize a wondrous world, a character's suffering, or a moment of pure joy. This active mental processing fundamentally boosts creative thinking. On the contrary, watching television is a passive experience where the visuals are merely the product of someone else’s imagination, leaving children to blindly observe what appears on the screen. Furthermore, while video games do require strategic thinking and tactics to win, these actions are driven by rule-based experience and problem-solving rather than genuine, spontaneous creativity.
In conclusion, I strongly believe that reading stories from a book is a far better pastime for children than watching TV or gaming. This is because literature demands active mental engagement that uniquely accelerates language development and unlocks true creative potential.

Tuy vậy, mở bài cần dùng mẫu nêu quan điểm Cô đã học thay vì chỉ viết I completely agree; em cũng cần viết đầy đủ television và chủ động luyện câu bị động ở những chỗ phù hợp. reviews.question:
Some people think that studying at university or college is the best way for students to prepare for their future career. Others, however, say today this is no longer true.
Discuss both views and give your opinion.
reviews.originalEssay:
Some people think students have the most solid foundation for future occupation when they pursue tertiary education, many others hold a reserve opinion, saying that this is not currently true. From my perspective, I am to advocate the latter stance.
Admittedly, university education is highly relevant to career preparation. Initially, according to this theory, it provides students with in-depth knowledge and qualifications in many professions, this can be easily seen in the way people find it impossible to become a doctor, a teacher or a lawyer without having the relevant degree. Furthermore, university education helps learners to develop high-level skills, say, critical thinking, independent research, structured communication, which are highly valued personal traits in many modern occupations.
However, I strongly believe tertiary education is far from a universally suitable or practical pathway for every student in today’s world. This can be easily seen in the way many young people, who struggle with abstract or theoretical knowledge, have talent in practical tasks. Vocational training, which is a more realistic and rewarding alternative, helps them gain hands-on experience and enter the workforce earlier in areas, say, construction, automotive repair or culinary arts. For example, a student with little academic interest but a passion for baking, finds greater success in a culinary school than in a university lecture hall.
In conclusion, the suitable education for a student must be determined on a case-by-case basis and a one-size-fit-all approach to education is hinder rather than help, which leads to wasted time and missed opportunities.
reviews.overall: Em giữ đúng hai mặt của đề và toàn bộ ý Cô giao. Em cần sửa vài câu để quan điểm, quy chiếu và cấu trúc chính xác hơn; bản sửa dưới đây vẫn giữ nguyên chuỗi ý của em.

reviews.suggestedRevision:
Some people believe that students can build the strongest foundation for their future careers by pursuing university or college education, whereas others argue that this is no longer necessarily true. From my perspective, I am firmly convinced that tertiary education is not the most suitable pathway for every young person.

Admittedly, university education is highly relevant to career preparation. Firstly, students are provided with in-depth knowledge and qualifications for many professions. This means that people cannot become doctors, teachers, or lawyers without the relevant degrees. Furthermore, university education helps learners develop high-level skills, such as critical thinking, independent research, and structured communication. These skills are highly valued in many modern occupations because they enable graduates to analyse problems and communicate their ideas effectively.

However, tertiary education is far from a universally suitable or practical pathway for every student in today's world. Many young people struggle with abstract or theoretical knowledge but have talent in practical tasks. For these individuals, vocational training is a more realistic and rewarding alternative because it enables them to gain hands-on experience and enter the workforce earlier in fields such as construction, automotive repair, or culinary arts. For example, a student with little academic interest but a passion for baking may find greater success in a culinary school than in a university lecture hall. Therefore, a suitable educational pathway should be chosen on a case-by-case basis. A one-size-fits-all approach to education hinders rather than helps, leading to wasted time and missed opportunities.

In conclusion, although university can prepare students well for many careers, it is not the best route for everyone. Students' strengths and interests should be considered when their educational paths are chosen.

reviews.question:
Too much emphasis is placed on going to university for academic education. People should be encouraged to do vocational training, because there is a lack of qualified tradespeople such as electricians or plumbers.
To what extent do you agree or disagree?
reviews.originalEssay:
There is an opinion that people nowadays pay too much attention to tertiary education, instead, they should be prompted to pursue vocational training areas, where they have limited skilled employees. Personally, however, I strongly believe that both university education and vocational training should be equally promoted.
On the one hand, higher education plays a critical role in building a highly skilled workforce, which is essential for key sectors of the national economy, say, healthcare, education, engineering, and technology. For example, doctors, who not only improve public health but also save thousands of lives or engineers and technicians contribute to national productivity and innovation. Therefore, without sufficient investment in higher education, countries would face a dearth of doctors, researchers, and policymakers, ultimately hindering national progress.
On the other hand, vocational training is equally important to society. Since not all young people are academically capable, it is a more realistic and rewarding alternative for them. It enables them to gain hands-on experience and enter the workforce earlier in areas, say, construction, automotive repair or culinary arts. Instead of blindly encouraging all students to pursue higher education, leading to wasted resources and youth unemployment, promoting vocational education as a viable and respectable path, which helps reduce graduate unemployment and ensures that all individuals are matched with careers that suit their strengths.

reviews.question:
The government should invest more money in teaching science than other subjects for a country’s development and progress.
To what extent do you agree or disagree?
reviews.originalEssay:
It is often argued that state funding should prioritize science education over other disciplines to foster national development. From my perspective, I partially agree with this statement, as the necessity of prioritizing science depends heavily on each country's specific circumstances.                                                                                                                                  On the one hand, for less technologically advanced nations, allocating more funds to science-related subjects is paramount to enhancing national productivity. With sufficient financial support, schools can equip modern laboratories and conduct regular scientific projects, which motivates more students to develop a keen interest in this field. Upon graduation, these individuals can become competent scientists, researchers, and skilled workers in key sectors of the economy such as agriculture, manufacturing, and healthcare. This robust workforce allows a developing nation to accelerate its economic progress, reduce dependence on foreign technologies, and bridge the developmental gap with global superpowers.
On the other hand, in more developed countries where science and technology are already strong, focusing too much on science education is unnecessary. Instead, these governments should apply a balanced investment approach across all subject groups. Developed nations often have to deal with complex societal problems such as social inequality, mental health crises, or a loss of cultural identity—issues that science alone cannot solve. Humanities such as history, literature, or ethics enable students to think deeply, understand different cultures, and better appreciate their own traditions and customs. Furthermore, other academic areas directly support science itself. For instance, ethics guides how new technology should be used in a fair and responsible way, while artistic thinking inspires innovation in science by offering fresh perspectives. If these areas are ignored, a country may grow quickly in terms of technology but will eventually become weak in culture and human connection.
In conclusion, I believe that while prioritizing investment in science education is a logical strategy for developing nations to progress economically, it should not be treated as a universal rule. Wealthier nations should maintain balanced funding across all disciplines to ensure a harmonious and balanced society.

Chuỗi tiền đầu tư → điều kiện học khoa học → nguồn nhân lực → phát triển kinh tế được giải thích mạch lạc. reviews.question:
Many people argue that in order to improve educational quality, high school students should be encouraged to make comments or even criticism on their teachers. Others; however, think it will lead to loss of respect and discipline in the classroom.
Discuss both views and give your opinion.
reviews.originalEssay:
Opinions are divided on whether high school students should be motivated to offer feedback and criticism on their teachers to enhance pedagogical quality, or if this practice would undermine classroom discipline. Regarding this, there is a strong case to be made for both sides of the debate.
On the one hand, supporters of student feedback often highlight that this practice gives teachers more chances to get to know their students. By receiving direct comments from learners, teachers become well-informed of their students' learning needs, allowing them to adopt or modify their teaching methods to meet those needs—a clear benefit to the progress of any student. They also claim that regular feedback from students prevents teachers from becoming complacent. Knowing that they will be evaluated regularly causes them to improve their teaching styles and methodologies continuously, leading to the enhancement of the teaching and learning environment as a whole.
On the other hand, though, advocates of classroom discipline often argue that some students may assess their teachers based on their own feelings and preferences rather than their teachers' contributions or techniques. On this side of the debate, people also emphasize that a student might evaluate their teacher’s performance as poor just because they do not like the teacher’s fashion style. Consequently, if massive numbers of comments from learners are introduced, opinions will vary from student to student, making it impossible for teachers to work out a way of teaching that satisfies all students and potentially throwing the classroom into chaos.
Overall, it appears that the stronger argument is in favor of encouraging student comments and criticism, with all the pronounced educational advantages of improving teaching methodologies and student progress. Of course, this is provided that these evaluations are conducted through a transparent and controlled system that promotes constructive feedback, thereby minimizing the potential risks of biased emotional judgments and maintaining mutual respect in the classroom.

reviews.question:
Schools are no longer necessary because children can get so much information available through the Internet, and they can study just as well at home.
To what extent do you agree or disagree?
reviews.originalEssay:
It is argued by some that the traditional school system has become redundant due to the vast abundance of educational information on the internet, which supposedly allows children to study effectively at home. I completely disagree with this viewpoint because access to information does not equate to effective learning, and the fundamental role of schools extends far beyond academic instruction.
On the one hand, while the internet has made educational content more accessible than ever before, it cannot replace the guidance of a formal school environment. Today, children can easily find video tutorials, e-books, and interactive learning tools on virtually any subject, often free of charge. For highly self-motivated learners, this flexibility serves as a valuable supplement to their studies. However, having access to information is not the same as knowing how to learn effectively. Young learners often lack the discipline, critical thinking skills, and time-management abilities required to navigate and organize information independently. Without professional guidance from trained teachers and the structure that schools provide, many students may become overwhelmed or misinformed, leading to a superficial or incorrect understanding of complex topics.
On the other hand, the holistic significance of attending school is irreplaceable. Although one of the main purposes of school is to provide academic instruction, its societal importance goes far beyond merely teaching facts or theories from textbooks. Schools provide a structured learning environment where students can develop essential life skills, such as teamwork, communication, and discipline. Furthermore, educational institutions serve as crucial social spaces where students learn to compete, cooperate, face challenges, and deal with a wide range of emotions. These real-life peer interactions help them grow emotionally and socially—something that simply cannot be gained by studying alone at home in front of a screen.
In conclusion, I strongly disagree with the notion that schools are no longer necessary. Despite the wealth of information available online, the structured guidance of teachers and the vital social environment of a physical classroom remain indispensable to a child’s comprehensive development.
reviews.overall: Em triển khai đúng hướng không đồng ý và giữ mạch lập luận rất rõ. Body 1 vừa thừa nhận ích lợi của Internet vừa giải thích vì sao thông tin không thay thế được việc học có hướng dẫn; Body 2 phát triển đúng vai trò xã hội và kỹ năng sống của trường học. reviews.question:
In today’s world of advanced science and technology, people still greatly value artists such as musicians, writers, and painters.
What can the arts tell us about life that science and technology cannot?
reviews.originalEssay:
Nowadays, artists such as musicians, writers and painters still gain great respect and admiration from the world, regardless of the prosperity of technology and science. Personally, I believe this is due to several undeniable advantages of the arts.
            Chief of them is that, arts excel in transmitting human emotions, something that science and technology often fail to capture. For example, the response of our body and train to nervousness and excitement is exactly the same , seen in the way our palms begin to sweat, how our hearts start to beat faster, and how adrenaline is produced in a certain region of the brain. But even the most advanced medical technologies such as MRI scanners, which could detail how our brain responds to external and internal cues, show identical results for these two feelings. This proves that science can not tell what a person is really going through, while arts can deliver such unique emotions. A song is able to express the joy of falling in love or the agony of heartbreak in a way that numbers and graphs can not, consequently it is not surprising that there are now billions of songs about love, yet each tells a different story and a different shade of feelings.
            Furthermore, arts provide insights into abstract human problems that remain unsolved by science. This can be easily seen in the way questions such as “ what is happiness” still puzzle psychoanalysts, philosophers, and scientists alike. In scientific terms, happiness is explained as the presence of certain conditions, say, personal achievement, material possessions, or stable relationships, while real life proves otherwise, as many individuals with fame, wealth, and seemingly perfect families still suffer from deep misery, sometimes even leading to suicide. This means that science struggles to explain this paradox, but writers, composers and painters have long portrayed such inner pain through poems, songs, and paintings. A common example is Billie Eilish, one of the most successful singers in the US, vividly conveyed her loneliness beneath glamour and success in When the party is over.
            In conclusion, I am strongly convinced that artists today are widely famous and play an important role in the community because of the importance of arts.
reviews.overall: Em đã triển khai đủ hai ý Cô giao: nghệ thuật truyền tải cảm xúc và khắc họa đời sống nội tâm, mỗi ý đều được so sánh với giới hạn của khoa học và có ví dụ. Cô yêu cầu em sửa mở bài và kết bài để trả lời thẳng nghệ thuật cho ta biết điều gì về cuộc sống, thay vì chỉ nói nghệ sĩ quan trọng. Bài này em soát chưa kỹ: train, câu ghép bằng dấu phẩy và câu Billie Eilish đều cần sửa. Giữ hai chuỗi giải thích đã viết khi chỉnh bài.

reviews.question:
Some people think history has nothing or little to tell us, but others think that studying the past can help us better understand the present.
Discuss both views and give your opinion.
reviews.originalEssay:
Opinions are divided on whether the study of history has lost its practical relevance in the modern era, or if it remains a vital tool for understanding the present. While I acknowledge the reasoning behind the former view due to rapid technological shifts, I strongly align with the latter stance, as the fundamental lessons of history are indispensable for navigating today's global complexities.
               On the one hand, it is understandable why some individuals believe history has little to offer contemporary society. They often argue that learning about historical events is merely a recording of facts from a bygone era, rendering such details only relevant to the specific context in which they occurred. Furthermore, given the unprecedented advancement of science and technology, today’s world has evolved drastically, making many past lessons seem obsolete. For example, military strategies utilized in ancient wars no longer apply to contemporary conflicts, which predominantly involve cyber-attacks, artificial intelligence, and economic sanctions rather than traditional physical battlefields. Consequently, from this perspective, insights gained from historical records can appear entirely disconnected from present-day realities.
                However, I strongly believe that these seemingly trivial historical facts actually provide invaluable lessons for today’s world, making the preservation of historical knowledge essential. By analyzing the root causes of past wars, modern society can effectively learn how to prevent conflicts and actively promote peace. Throughout history, various civilizations invaded one another under the false belief that they could only prosper at the expense of others. History has fundamentally debunked this notion, proving that global cooperation, rather than armed conflict, is essential for sustained national growth. Moreover, the past explicitly demonstrates that wars bring nothing but severe economic losses, stemming not only from the sheer cost of weaponry but also from the catastrophic decline in overall economic activity. This profound insight perfectly explains why large-scale wars have become rare today, as almost every modern leader strives for peace and political stability to secure their nation’s prosperity—a valuable fruit that can only be harvested by studying the past.
               In conclusion, although the argument regarding technological changes making ancient strategies obsolete carries some weight, it is overshadowed by the enduring value of historical insights. I am completely convinced that studying the past is far from useless; rather, it is a crucial guide that helps humankind understand the mechanisms of peace, economic stability, and international cooperation in the present day.
reviews.overall: Em đã bàn đủ hai quan điểm, giữ lập trường rõ và phát triển gần trọn chuỗi ý Cô giao. Body 1 giải thích vì sao một số người thấy lịch sử ít hữu ích; Body 2 nối nguyên nhân chiến tranh với giá trị của hợp tác và hòa bình. Cuối Body 2, “a valuable fruit” đang gắn với sự thịnh vượng của quốc gia, làm lệch ý cần chốt: chính hiểu biết rút ra từ quá khứ là thành quả của việc học lịch sử. Em sửa câu này rồi đọc lại mối liên hệ giữa các ý.

reviews.question:
Most people have forgotten the meaning behind traditional or religious festivals; during festival periods, people nowadays only want to enjoy themselves.
To what extent do you agree or disagree with this opinion?
reviews.originalEssay:
It is often argued that the profound significance of traditional and religious festivals has largely faded from public consciousness, with modern celebrations shifting toward pure self-indulgence and recreation. I completely agree with this viewpoint, as the historical origins of these holidays are increasingly misunderstood, and their observation has degenerated into opportunities for personal entertainment.
           On the one hand, the underlying meaning of cultural and religious festivals has largely been forgotten by contemporary society. Today, many individuals participate in age-old rituals without understanding their historical or spiritual roots. For example, Vietnamese people interpret the meaning of specific activities during Tet very differently across generations. Younger generations often think that giving money to children in this holiday is merely a token of good luck. However, this interpretation is far from the historical truth. Traditionally, giving money to children was practiced to protect them from lost souls, as the money was intended to act as a symbolic bribe so that malevolent spirits would not harm the children. This clear disconnect highlights how original cultural narratives have been lost over time.
           On the other hand, religious and traditional festivals have increasingly become times for mere celebration and personal gratification. In the past, these periods demanded active community engagement and familial duties; however, people nowadays prioritize individual enjoyment. In Vietnam, Tet used to be a festive period when families spent considerable time shopping, meticulously decorating their homes, and enjoying traditional meals together to honor their ancestors. Conversely, most young Vietnamese people now look forward to Tet primarily as an occasion to have fun or simply as a long holiday period, rather than a time to engage in traditional activities. For instance, many of them consider going to temples to pray for good fortune, or asking for old-school calligraphy, as a fun leisure activity rather than a solemn religious observance. Furthermore, many others decide to go on a vacation trip during this time instead of enjoying their families' company, cementing the transition of festivals into commercialized holidays.
              In conclusion, I strongly agree that the authentic spirit of traditional and religious festivals is dying out. Not only has the true symbolic meaning behind ancient customs been forgotten, but the modern way of life has also reoriented these sacred occasions into commercialized periods dedicated strictly to personal leisure and entertainment.
reviews.overall: Em đã trả lời cả hai vế của đề và triển khai đủ các ví dụ về Tết theo dàn ý. Cô ghi nhận cách em dùng “often”, câu bị động và các từ nối để dẫn người đọc qua hai thân bài. Em cần sửa những chỗ khẳng định quá mức: việc đi du lịch dịp Tết cho thấy xu hướng hưởng thụ cá nhân, chưa chứng minh lễ hội đã bị thương mại hóa. Em cũng cần dùng “observance” khi nói về việc thực hành lễ hội và trình bày chuyện tiền mừng tuổi như một cách lý giải truyền thống.

Viết về các gia đình trong dịp Tết trước đây và “many young people” hiện nay.

anchors.quote: In the past, these periods demanded active community engagement and familial duties; however, people nowadays prioritize individual enjoyment.

annotations.label: a6
annotations.title: Giữ chi tiết đúng dàn ý
annotations.bodyMarkdown:
Dàn ý nêu các gia đình ăn bữa truyền thống cùng nhau, chưa giao mục đích này. Nếu không giải thích thêm, em chỉ cần giữ hoạt động ăn cùng gia đình.

Kết câu ở “enjoying traditional meals together”.

anchors.quote: to honor their ancestors

annotations.label: a7
annotations.title: Bỏ từ lặp nghĩa
annotations.bodyMarkdown:
“Vacation” và “trip” ở đây trùng ý, không làm ví dụ rõ hơn.

Dùng “trip” hoặc “travel during Tet”.

anchors.quote: vacation trip

annotations.label: a8
annotations.title: Kết quả không theo ví dụ
annotations.bodyMarkdown:
Đi du lịch thay vì ở bên gia đình cho thấy xu hướng hưởng thụ cá nhân; câu trước chưa nói về quảng cáo, mua bán hay hoạt động kinh doanh để kết luận “commercialized”. Cụm V-ing “cementing” nối đúng hình thức nhưng quan hệ nhân–quả chưa đúng.

Viết “showing how these celebrations may shift toward individual leisure”; bỏ “commercialized” ở kết bài.

anchors.quote: cementing the transition of festivals into commercialized holidays

annotations.label: a9
annotations.title: Kết bài cần khớp mức độ chứng minh
annotations.bodyMarkdown:
Bài chứng minh cách hiểu cũ có thể phai nhạt và việc vui chơi được chú trọng hơn, chưa chứng minh toàn bộ tinh thần lễ hội sắp biến mất.

Viết “is less widely understood” và nhắc cả sự chuyển sang vui chơi cá nhân.

anchors.quote: is dying out

reviews.suggestedRevision:
It is often argued that the original significance of traditional and religious festivals has largely faded from public consciousness, while many people now treat these occasions mainly as times for enjoyment. I am firmly convinced that both parts of this view are largely accurate: the meanings of some long-standing customs are less widely understood, and individual leisure has become a stronger focus during festival periods.

On the one hand, the original meaning of many cultural and religious festivals is no longer widely understood. Today, many individuals participate in age-old rituals without knowing their historical or spiritual roots. For example, Vietnamese people can interpret Tet customs differently across generations. Younger people often regard giving children money during Tet simply as a token of good luck. Yet one traditional explanation presents this money as protection against lost souls: it was believed to act as a symbolic bribe so that malevolent spirits would not harm children. The difference between these interpretations shows how an older cultural explanation can fade even when the custom itself continues.

On the other hand, these festivals are increasingly treated as occasions for personal enjoyment. In Vietnam, Tet used to involve families spending time shopping, decorating their homes, and sharing traditional meals. Many young Vietnamese people now look forward to Tet mainly as a chance to have fun or take a long break, rather than to engage in these activities. Some may treat going to temples to pray for good fortune or asking for traditional calligraphy as leisure activities rather than focusing on their religious or cultural meaning. Furthermore, others go on a trip during Tet instead of spending time with their families. These examples suggest a shift from shared customs toward individual leisure.

In conclusion, I strongly believe that many people are losing sight of the meanings of traditional and religious festivals, while festival periods are increasingly used for personal enjoyment. The Tet examples show how customs can continue even as their original explanations and family activities receive less attention.

“Often” giữ mức độ phù hợp, và bản sửa dùng cấu trúc khác để diễn đạt lại cách hiểu của người trẻ.
Câu mở đoạn của em bao quát đúng vai trò Body 1; bản sửa giữ chức năng đó và nói rõ phạm vi “many”.
Em đã nêu rõ mức độ đồng ý với hai vế; bản sửa minh họa một cách diễn đạt quan điểm đã học và gắn trực tiếp với cả hai thay đổi.
nextSteps: Sửa câu kết Body 2 và kết bài: ví dụ đi du lịch chỉ chứng minh sự chú trọng vui chơi cá nhân, không chứng minh thương mại hóa.
Soát các khẳng định rộng như “people nowadays” và “dying out”; giới hạn về nhiều người trẻ, dịp Tết hoặc xu hướng khi ví dụ chỉ hỗ trợ đến đó.
Đổi “observation” thành “observance” hoặc dùng “observe”, rồi đọc lại các cụm thừa như “vacation trip”.
